Define a custom deterministic scanner

Source: R/scanner.R
scanner.Rd

scanner() wraps a plain function and the facts the assessment contract needs: a name, a version, the evidence it requires, and its settings. Pass scanners to scan_trajectories(), assess_trajectory_scans(), investigation_snapshot(), scans_tools(), or scans_app() through their scanners argument. Nothing is registered globally: a scanner exists only for the calls it is passed to.

Usage

scanner(
  name,
  fn,
  description,
  required_evidence,
  version = "1",
  severity = "warning",
  settings = list()
)

scanner_findings(
  event_id = NA_character_,
  label = character(),
  explanation = character(),
  turn_id = NA_character_,
  event_ids = NULL,
  value = NULL
)

scanner_unassessed(status, reason)

Arguments

name

One scanner name: lower-case letters, digits, and underscores, starting with a letter. It must not be the name of a built-in scan in scan_registry().

fn

A function of trajectory and settings. It must be deterministic and must not call a model or tool.

description

One sentence describing what a finding means.

required_evidence

One sentence naming the recorded evidence the scanner needs before it can assess a trajectory.

version

One non-empty version string. Change it whenever fn or its meaning changes; it is recorded with every finding and assessment.

severity

"warning" or "error", applied to every finding.

settings

A named list of data passed to fn and recorded with each assessment, such as tool names or phrases the application owner chose. It must hold only data a saved investigation can store: no functions, environments, or objects of other classes.

event_id, turn_id

Primary evidence identities for each finding, from the scanned trajectory. NA means the finding has none. A finding with an event and no turn takes the event's turn; one with both must name the event's own turn.

label, explanation

A short label and a one-sentence explanation for each finding. All arguments are recycled to a common size with the vctrs rules: only length one recycles, and other mismatches are an error.

event_ids

Optional list with every supporting event identifier for each finding. The primary event is always included.

value

Optional list of scan-specific structured details, one per finding. Like settings, it must hold only data a saved investigation can store; otherwise the result is an execution failure.

status

"insufficient_evidence" or "not_applicable".

reason

One sentence, at most 500 characters, saying what is missing or why the scan does not apply. It is shown with the assessment.

Value

scanner() returns a scans_scanner value.

scanner_findings() returns a tibble of findings of class scans_scanner_findings; call it with no arguments for a clean negative. scanner_unassessed() returns a value that marks the trajectory as not assessed.

Details

fn is called once per trajectory as fn(trajectory, settings). trajectory is a list holding one trajectory's rows from the bundle accessors: trajectory_id, info (one row of trajectory_info()), turns (in turn order), events (in event order), evaluations, and losses (the trajectory_losses() rows assigned to this trajectory or to no trajectory). It must return one of:

  • scanner_findings(): the scanner assessed the trajectory. Return scanner_findings() with no arguments to say "assessed, no findings" (assessed_no_findings).

  • scanner_unassessed(): the scanner could not assess the trajectory, because the evidence it needs is not recorded ("insufficient_evidence") or the scan does not apply to this capture ("not_applicable").

Anything else, including NULL and a data frame not made by scanner_findings() (even an empty one), is an execution failure rather than a clean negative, so a scanner that forgets to return cannot report "no findings". Rows can be dropped from a scanner_findings() result with [. The scanner decides whether recorded losses prevent an assessment; the framework lists them in the assessment's limitations.

The framework checks every finding. A turn or event reference that is not in the scanned trajectory, a primary event outside the finding's turn, or a malformed finding, makes the whole result an execution_failure for that scanner and trajectory, and none of its findings are kept. A scanner that throws an error, or raises any other condition with stop(), is an execution_failure for that scanner and trajectory only. Warnings and messages are not failures and pass through. assess_trajectory_scans() records a fixed reason and never copies the condition message; scan_trajectories() re-signals the failure with the original condition as its parent.

Finding identifiers are <scan_id>/<name>/finding-<n>, numbered per scanner in bundle trajectory order, then by the primary event, then in the order returned. They do not change when other scanners are added, removed, or deselected, and built-in identifiers never change because a custom scanner ran.

Examples

no_apology <- scanner(
  "apology_without_action",
  function(trajectory, settings) {
    events <- trajectory$events
    roles <- trajectory$turns$role[
      match(events$turn_id, trajectory$turns$turn_id)
    ]
    answers <- events[roles %in% "assistant" & events$event_type == "content", ]
    if (nrow(answers) == 0L) {
      return(scanner_unassessed(
        "insufficient_evidence",
        "No assistant text is recorded."
      ))
    }
    hits <- answers[grepl(settings$phrase, answers$text, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
    scanner_findings(
      event_id = hits$event_id,
      label = rep("Apology", nrow(hits)),
      explanation = rep("The assistant apologised.", nrow(hits))
    )
  },
  description = "The assistant apologised.",
  required_evidence = "Recorded assistant text.",
  settings = list(phrase = "sorry")
)

bundle <- TrajectoryBundle(
  data.frame(trajectory_id = "run-1", source_type = "manual"),
  data.frame(trajectory_id = "run-1", turn_id = "turn-1", turn_index = 1L,
             role = "assistant"),
  data.frame(trajectory_id = "run-1", event_id = "event-1", event_index = 1L,
             turn_id = "turn-1", event_type = "content",
             text = "Sorry about that.")
)
result <- assess_trajectory_scans(
  bundle,
  scans = "apology_without_action",
  scanners = list(no_apology)
)
result$assessments[c("scan", "scan_version", "status")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   scan                   scan_version status                
#>   <chr>                  <chr>        <chr>                 
#> 1 apology_without_action 1            assessed_with_findings
result$findings[c("finding_id", "event_id", "label")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   finding_id                                        event_id label  
#>   <chr>                                             <chr>    <chr>  
#> 1 scan-000001/apology_without_action/finding-000001 event-1  Apology
